messages:
incident-bot: pagerduty triggered a page for service=Inference Gateway environment=prod-us-east-1 severity=high — 5xx rate >= 6% over 5m, total requests affected ~1.2k. Pager: oncall-infra -> @devon. runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/inference-5xx

pagerduty: INC#2003456 — page fired, urgency: high, escalation: automated (15m)

devon: ack. i'm on it. looking at dashboards now :mag_right:

devon: quick data point — gateway error-rate graph shows a sharp ramp at 13:42 UTC, per-az breakdown: us-east1-b worst, us-east1-a elevated, eu-west1 minimal

sam: also seeing a correlated bump in request latency right before the 5xx spike, might be overload/backpressure on upstream model replicas

ashley: tagging in SRE for infra-side mitigations. @devon @sam can you paste recent logs from gateway (5xx ranges)?

devon: paste log snippet:
```
2026-03-14T13:42:11Z GET /v1/generate 502 upstream_error model-v2-replica-5 latency=1534ms
2026-03-14T13:42:12Z POST /v1/chat 503 kv-cache-miss model-v2-replica-7 oom? memory_pressure=85%
2026-03-14T13:42:13Z GET /v1/generate 500 runtime-exec-failed model-quant-a seq=64
```

ashley: those OOM-ish / memory_pressure lines stand out. could be a bad quant build or a recent rollout?

sam: I rolled a small patch to model routing yesterday afternoon — it shouldn't touch quant flags, but there was a kernel tweak on the runtime nodes that landed in us-east yesterday. tagging infra-runtime: @kevin

kevin: saw the runtime kernel tweak in us-east pool, good catch. rolling back the kernel tweak on a canary now. will update within ~8m.

devon: in parallel i'm temporarily shifting traffic away from us-east1-b to the warm pool in us-east1-c and enabling fallback routing to model-v2-degraded for short requests. commands run:
```
# shift 30% traffic off us-east1-b
redwood route update --service inference-gateway --from-zone us-east1-b --to-zone us-east1-c --percent 30
# enable degraded fallback policy
redwood routing set-fallback --service inference-gateway --model model-v2-degraded --threshold 3%
```

pagerduty: escalation scheduled in 15m if no ack from second-level. current status: ack by devon; SRE on-call engaged (ashley)

ashley: I'm scaling up gateway replicas in us-east by +20% and draining the worst hosts. also opening a temporary autoscale policy to speed up. monitoring CPU/RAM on replicas.

sam: after routing shift the 5xx rate in us-east1-b dropped from 6.4% -> 2.1% in the next 90s. latency also trending down. looks promising.

devon: runtime canary rollback succeeded on the first 3 nodes, will continue until 10 nodes checked. no obvious errors post-rollback so far.

kevin: can we confirm customer impact? any large customers seeing failed requests or support tickets?

ashley: initial logs show errors were evenly distributed across orgs but heavier on high-concurrency streams. support: no external tickets yet, we did surface a transient increase in 5xx to top-10 customers — ops notified them via status page.

devon: status page update posted: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/2003456 — brief note about degraded performance, mitigation in flight :information_source:

sam: running healthcheck script across model replicas now. results: 4 replicas returned non-healthy and were auto-drained. they had older quant build type B; rolling to type A in progress.

devon: keeping page pinned. if the rollback + routing holds for 20m i'll hand back to postmortem/infra and close. anyone want to escalate to on-call SRE manager?

kevin: not yet, we should let current mitigations finish. good job triaging. next: postmortem with root cause traffic + kernel tweak + quant mismatch.

incident-bot: pagerduty note — escalation suppressed (acknowledged). auto-reminder set for 20m.

devon: closing the active page in 22m if metrics stay stable. opening follow-up ticket INC-2003456-PM for postmortem and assign to devon+sre+runtime.

ashley: logging notes to runbook: add step to verify kernel tweak compatibility with quant builds before rollout.

kevin: thanks everyone. monitoring until stable, will deputize if it regresses. :thumbsup:
